risks: R1: howto.md is referenced as the single source of truth for ALL content (commands, gotchas, warnings, tips, examples, YouTube links, version badges, pipeline diagram) but is NOT provided in the task spec. Implementation is impossible without it — engineers will fabricate content or block.
R2: 'Copy every command verbatim from howto.md' combined with no howto.md means there is zero verifiable content contract. Any review would be comparing output against a phantom document.

R3: SOP mandates 'All functions must have at least one test' — for a 13-page static documentation site with React components, this implies substantial test scaffolding. Testing verbatim content correctness against howto.md programmatically requires that howto.md be parseable or its content be encoded as test fixtures. No guidance on how content fidelity is tested.

R4: SOP mandates files under 300 lines. Several pages may have extensive CLI command blocks, gotchas, and examples copied verbatim from howto.md. A single page component could easily exceed 300 lines if the source content is large, forcing arbitrary splitting with no clear decomposition strategy.

R5: YouTube embed URLs require specific video IDs. If howto.md links are standard youtube.com/watch?v= URLs, they must be transformed to youtube.com/embed/ format. If the links are missing or broken, the feature is undeliverable.

R6: 'Version badges showing component versions' — source of version data is completely unspecified. Are versions hardcoded? Read from package.json files? Fetched from an API? This is a static site with 'no backend required' so dynamic fetching is contradictory.

R7: Single-page application with 13 'pages' implies client-side routing. Vercel deployment of an SPA requires rewrite rules (all paths → index.html) or the build must handle this. No mention of routing library or Vercel config.
R8: The pipeline diagram on the Home page is referenced but not described. Is it an image asset from howto.md? An SVG? A React component rendering a flowchart? Format and source are unspecified.

R9: Tailwind CSS with Vite requires specific configuration (postcss.config, tailwind.config). The spec doesn't mention any starter template or existing scaffolding — risk of config mismatch across engineers.
ambiguities: A1: Routing strategy — is this hash-based routing (#/step-0-cartographer), browser history routing (/step-0-cartographer), or a single scrollable page with anchor sections? 'Single-page React application' with 'Navigation between pages' is contradictory without clarification.
A2: URL slug naming convention for each page is unspecified. Different engineers will produce different slugs (e.g., 'step-0-cartographer' vs 'cartographer' vs 'step0' vs '0-cartographer').
A3: 'Embed YouTube videos linked in howto.md for each step' — does 'each step' mean every page gets a video, or only pages where howto.md contains a video link? What if some steps have no video?
A4: Navigation UX — sidebar, top nav bar, breadcrumbs, next/prev buttons? No design spec or wireframe provided.
A5: 'Version badges showing component versions' — badge visual style (shields.io-style, custom, npm badge)? Per-page or global? What components have versions?
A6: Mobile responsiveness requirements are not stated. Tailwind implies responsive design intent but no breakpoints or behavior is specified.
A7: The pact.yaml specifies vitest but doesn't specify what contract tests exist or what the test targets are. Are there pre-existing contract tests to satisfy, or must they be authored from scratch?
A8: Code syntax highlighting for CLI command blocks — is a library like Prism or Shiki expected, or plain <pre><code> blocks?
A9: Does 'all content must be exact as in howto.md' mean Markdown rendering of the howto.md content, or manual JSX transcription of each section?
questions: Q1: Where is howto.md? Is it in a repository, provided as an artifact, or expected to be read from a specific path at build time? Without it, no implementation can begin.
Q2: What routing library should be used — react-router-dom, or another approach? Should routes use hash-based or history-based navigation?
Q3: What are the exact URL slugs for each of the 13 pages?
Q4: Where do component version numbers come from? Are they hardcoded strings, read from a manifest, or dynamically fetched?
Q5: What is the pipeline diagram — an image file, an SVG, or a programmatically rendered component? Where is the source asset?
Q6: Should howto.md be parsed at build time (Markdown → React) or should its content be manually transcribed into JSX components?
Q7: Are there existing contract tests (pact tests) that this implementation must satisfy, or are tests authored as part of this task?
Q8: Is there a design system, color palette, or visual reference for the site, or is the implementer free to choose within Tailwind defaults?
Q9: For the SOP rule 'All functions must have at least one test' — does this apply to every React component (rendering tests), or only to utility/logic functions?
Q10: Does the site need to handle deep-link navigation on Vercel (i.e., vercel.json rewrites), or is hash routing acceptable?
assumptions: AS1: howto.md will be provided as an input artifact before implementation begins; it is not expected to be generated.
AS2: Client-side routing via react-router-dom with history-based navigation will be used, with a vercel.json rewrite rule for SPA fallback.
AS3: URL slugs will follow the pattern: /, /step-0-cartographer, /step-1a-constrain, /step-1b-ledger, etc.
AS4: Version badges are hardcoded strings extracted from howto.md, not dynamically fetched.
AS5: The pipeline diagram is a static visual (SVG or image) that will be provided or extracted from howto.md.
AS6: Navigation will be a persistent sidebar with links to all 13 pages.
AS7: Content from howto.md will be manually transcribed into JSX components (not parsed at build time from Markdown).
AS8: Every React component gets a basic rendering smoke test via @testing-library/react to satisfy the SOP testing requirement.
AS9: Code blocks for CLI commands use a syntax highlighting library (e.g., prism-react-renderer) with copy-to-clipboard functionality, since developers are expected to copy-paste.
AS10: The site is desktop-first but must be responsive down to tablet width (768px). No mobile-specific UX is required.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: Project scaffolded in exemplar-tools-doc/ with TypeScript, Vite, React, Tailwind CSS. All source files are .ts or .tsx — zero .py or .js source files.
AC2: `npm install && npm run dev` starts a dev server on port 4000 without errors.
AC3: `npm run build` produces a production build with zero TypeScript errors and zero warnings.
AC4: All 13 pages (Home + 12 step pages) are navigable via client-side routing. Direct URL access to any route renders the correct page (Vercel SPA fallback configured).
AC5: Every CLI command on each page matches the corresponding command in howto.md character-for-character. A diff of extracted commands against howto.md produces zero differences.
AC6: Every gotcha, warning, tip, and example from howto.md is present on the corresponding page, verbatim.
AC7: YouTube videos from howto.md are embedded as iframes on their respective pages and are playable.
AC8: Version badges are displayed for each component that has a version in howto.md.
AC9: The Home page displays the pipeline diagram.
AC10: `npm run test` executes vitest and all tests pass. Every exported function/component has at least one test.
AC12: All exports follow SOP conventions: named exports on all functions/types/constants; React components have both named and default exports; every .tsx file imports React.
AC13: `npx vercel --prod` deploys successfully and the deployed site is navigable.
AC14: No Python files exist anywhere in the output.
AC15: CLI command blocks have a copy-to-clipboard affordance (button or interaction) so developers can copy-paste commands.

pause_reason: Phase cycle limit reached (34 diagnose cycles, max=3). Human review required.
